RFB.description:
RF Band Specification

UNITS ARE NORMATIVE. Every frequency field in this table is MHz. Sources
that publish Hz (as open transmitter databases commonly do) MUST divide by
1e6 before encoding; sources
that publish kHz MUST divide by 1e3. BAUD is baud (symbols per second),
never kilobaud. Encoding a Hz value into a MHz field is a defect, not a
convention.

One RFB record carries exactly one LINK_DIRECTION. A transceiver or
transponder is therefore represented as TWO RFB records — one UPLINK and
one DOWNLINK — sharing ID_TRANSMITTER, each carrying its own MODE,
FREQ_MIN, FREQ_MAX and CENTER_FREQ.

NORAD_CAT_ID.description:
NORAD catalog number of the spacecraft carrying this emitter. Joins to
CAT.NORAD_CAT_ID. 0 when unbound.

ID_TRANSMITTER.description:
Identifier of the physical transmitter, transceiver or transponder this
record describes (e.g. an upstream transmitter database's UUID). Uplink
and downlink
records of the same device share this value.

LINK_DIRECTION.description: Direction of this emission relative to the spacecraft.

BAUD.description: Symbol rate in baud (symbols per second), NOT kilobaud.

SERVICE.description: Regulatory/ITU service designation (e.g. Amateur, Earth Exploration).

INVERT.description: True when the modulation sideband is inverted.

IARU_COORDINATION.description: IARU frequency-coordination state (e.g. IARU Coordinated, Uncoordinated).

CITATION.description:
Attribution/citation string the source license requires this record to
carry downstream.

RFSFrequencySample.description:
The material's electromagnetic properties at ONE frequency. A table of
these beats the power-law fit wherever it covers the frequency.

FREQUENCY_MHZ.description:
Frequency this sample is stated at, megahertz — the `$RFB` MHz
convention. A join to `$IQC` (hertz) converts explicitly at the join.

RELATIVE_PERMITTIVITY_REAL.description: Real part of the relative permittivity.

RELATIVE_PERMITTIVITY_IMAGINARY.description:
Imaginary part of the relative permittivity (loss term), stated as a
POSITIVE magnitude.

RELATIVE_PERMEABILITY_REAL.description:
Real and imaginary relative permeability. 1.0 and 0.0 for non-magnetic
materials — stated, not assumed.

REFLECTIVITY.description: Power reflected at normal incidence as a ratio [0-1].

REFLECTION_LOSS_DB.description: Reflection loss at normal incidence, dB (positive).

TRANSMISSION_LOSS_DB.description: Loss through the material at THICKNESS_M, dB (positive).

ATTENUATION_DB_PER_M.description: Attenuation inside the material, dB per metre.

RFSReflectionEntry.description:
Reflection and transmission at one incidence angle and polarization. The
angular dependence of a real surface cannot be carried by a single
normal-incidence number.

FREQUENCY_MHZ.description: Frequency this entry is stated at, megahertz.

INCIDENCE_ANGLE_DEG.description: Angle from the surface normal, degrees [0-90).

TRANSVERSE_ELECTRIC.description: Electric field perpendicular to the plane of incidence.

TRANSVERSE_MAGNETIC.description: Electric field parallel to the plane of incidence.

REFLECTION_COEFFICIENT_MAGNITUDE.description: Magnitude of the field reflection coefficient [0-1].

REFLECTION_COEFFICIENT_PHASE_DEG.description: Phase of the field reflection coefficient, degrees.

TRANSMISSION_LOSS_DB.description: Loss through the material at this angle, dB (positive).

SCATTERING_LOSS_DB.description: Power removed from the specular direction by surface roughness, dB.

RFSGeometryRef.description:
Where and what this material is attached to. A material record with no
geometry describes a substance; a material record WITH geometry describes
an obstacle a solver can intersect.

FEATURE_ID.description: Producer's own feature identifier for a building, wall or terrain patch.

ANALYTIC_SHAPE.description:
Primitive and its dimensions in metres, when GEOMETRY_KIND is
ANALYTIC_SHAPE. The dimension order is the primitive's own convention and
MUST be stated in SHAPE_DIMENSION_NAMES.

CONVEX_HULL.description: Convex hull of a point set carried by the geometry it references.

NORMAL_AZIMUTH_DEG.description:

horizon. A wall that faces the wrong way blocks the wrong link.
